title: Why BPA-Free Receipt Paper Matters for Hospitality Staff
description: Servers and bartenders handle receipts all day. Here's why BPA-free thermal paper is a safer, smarter choice for your team and guests.
body:
Your staff touch receipts dozens of times a shift — ringing up orders, closing tabs, printing kitchen tickets. If those receipts are printed on traditional thermal paper, your team is handling the same chemical coating every single time. Switching to BPA-free thermal paper is a low-effort change that shows your people you're paying attention to the details.

What's on a traditional thermal receipt?

Thermal paper doesn't use ink. It's coated with a heat-reactive layer that darkens when it passes under the print head. For years, most of that coating used BPA (bisphenol A) as a developer — a compound that helps the paper react to heat and produce sharp, dark text.

That coating can transfer to skin on contact, and receipts get handled constantly in a hospitality setting. BPA-free paper swaps the developer for an alternative (commonly BPS or a phenol-free formulation) while keeping the same crisp, fast printing you rely on at the point of sale.

Why it matters in hospitality specifically

  • Constant contact. Servers, bartenders, and cashiers handle receipts far more often than a typical shopper does. Cumulative, all-day exposure is the real concern.
  • Wet hands and handling. Behind a bar, receipts get touched with damp hands, which can make the coating transfer more readily than dry handling.
  • Guest-facing moments. The receipt goes straight into a guest's hands, often right after a meal or drink. It's one more touchpoint where the quality of what you hand over reflects on your business.

Does it print the same?

For the vast majority of modern thermal printers, BPA-free paper prints with the same density and speed as traditional rolls. The difference you might notice is slightly different image durability over the long term — some phenol-free papers can fade a bit faster when exposed to heat or sunlight — but for a standard receipt that's read and discarded, that difference is rarely meaningful.

Before switching, check your printer model's recommended paper specs. Most current Epson, Star, and Bixolon POS printers handle BPA-free stock without any adjustment.

What to look for when ordering

  • Verify the label. Look for "BPA-free" or "phenol-free" on the spec sheet — not just "eco-friendly," which can be vague.
  • Match the roll size. Confirm width (typically 80mm or 57mm), core size, and roll diameter so the new stock fits your printer drawer without jamming.
  • Match the coating. If you have a specific print quality requirement (kitchen tickets that must survive heat and grease), test a roll before committing your whole operation.

Conclusion

BPA-free receipt paper is a simple, honest upgrade for hospitality teams that handle receipts constantly. It prints reliably in most modern POS printers, removes a common chemical from daily handling, and sends a clear signal to your staff that their comfort matters.
